Subject: Private deploy sizing kickoff — network diagram attached

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for taking this on. We're trying to lock down sizing and the procurement path for a private VPC deployment (on-prem with VPC peering to our colo). Attached is our network layout (novus_network_layout_v1.pdf) and a short inventory of expected traffic patterns. High level:
- Target production date: Q4 2028
- Expected steady-state: ~140 concurrent inference sessions, avg 320 tokens per request
- Peak window: ~12pm-2pm local, 3x steady-state for ~30 minutes

Primary asks:
1) A recommended baseline GPU pool size (with headroom) and a brief explanation of the tradeoffs.
2) Network/egress guidance (eg: NICs, cross-connects, egress shaping) we should plan for.
3) A procurement-friendly mutual action plan or checklist so our procurement team can map out PO and timelines.

We'd like to include EdgeOps (our colo integrator) on the thread to align on cross-connects and cabling.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan

Subject: Re: Private deploy sizing kickoff — network diagram attached

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the diagram and the traffic notes. Quick read and a first-pass recommendation below so procurement can start aligning timelines. I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan document and a rough cost band. Jonas and Mina are cc'd for technical sizing and warmup/cache considerations.

High-level assumptions (please confirm):
- Baseline workload: 140 concurrent sessions, avg 320 tokens/session, 3-second avg think time -> roughly 15–20 RPS sustained (depending on request batching).
- Model baseline for sizing: Llama-2-13B quantized (we use this as a conservative compute baseline); if you plan to run a heavier family we should re-run estimates.

First-pass recommendation:
- Baseline pool: 6 x H100-class GPUs for steady-state (supports target qps with ~20% headroom for cache misses).
- Peak/Buffering: add a burst pool of 3 GPUs that can be brought online for scheduled windows (autoscale with warm-pool pre-warm).
- Minimum total initial commit: 8 GPU equivalents (we size for 9 physical GPUs to leave one spare for maintenance).

Why this split: 6 handles steady traffic with conservative KV cache hit assumptions; 3-burst lets you absorb 3x short peaks without impacting tail latency. The spare node buys you rolling updates and quick failover.

Network guidance:
- Request a dual 100Gbps cross-connect to your primary colo VLAN for control+data separation.
- Use a dedicated east-west VLAN for GPU traffic; avoid NAT for pod-to-pod KV cache access.
- Egress shaping: plan for an average outbound of ~400–600 Mbps (model weights, embeddings shipping, logs). We recommend a per-GPU NIC allocation of 40–60Gbps headroom during redistribution/eviction storms.

Operational notes:
- KV cache warmup: allow ~8–10 minutes warmup for cold workloads; our warm-pool flow will pre-populate cache for scheduled peaks.
- Autoscale: prefer scheduled ramp + reactive autoscale with a 30s admission-delay to avoid oscillation.

Attachments I will add: MAP_Novus_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones), rough_throughput_estimates.csv (per-variant sizing numbers).

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm model family and expected average seq length (320 tokens is assumed).
- Confirm whether you need dedicated tenant isolation (single-tenant physical carveout) or multi-tenant within your VPC.
- Procurement: Samira, if you share the internal PO/contract timeline, Marissa will map an onboarding milestone plan.

Onwards —
Elliot 
Elliot Price
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Samira / Novus procurement team —

Looping in procurement steps and a short checklist you can use when running the PO process. High level timeline we typically see: 2–4 weeks for commercial review + PO issuance, 2–6 weeks for cross-connect scheduling with colo, and 3–4 weeks for Redwood Private install & acceptance (parallelized when possible).

Quick procurement checklist (we've attached a MAP):
- Review SOW: includes hardware carveout, network requirements, initial commit (9 GPUs), and warm-pool config.
- Security Annex: KMS/HSM integration options and SOC2 report (we'll provide evidence).
- SLA Appendix: agreed latency SLOs and throughput commitments; we will define rollback/fallback behavior.
- PO: please reference deal id NR-2028-047 and indicate target ship date for onboarding.

Cost bands (preliminary):
- Option A (committed 9 GPUs, 36-month): price band $X,XXX,XXX — includes priority onboarding, 6 month warm pool support.
- Option B (committed 6 GPUs + burst 3 via reserved flex, 24-month): price band $X,XXX,XXX — lower commit term, slightly higher unit cost.

If you can share your preferred procurement cadence and any legal timelines, we can prepare a final SOW and DocuSign link.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
